title: Count Square Submatrices with All Ones
summary: Provide the count of square submatrices within a m * n grid that consist entirely of ones.
statement: Provide the count of square submatrices within a m * n grid that consist entirely of ones.
constraints: Count square submatrices of every size.
hints: Let dp[j] be the largest all-one square ending at the current cell.
For a one, use one plus the minimum of upper, left, and upper-left sizes.
Add every ending size to the answer because it represents that many nested squares.
A larger square exists exactly when all three smaller neighboring squares exist.
editorial: A larger square exists exactly when all three smaller neighboring squares exist.

tests.explanation: There are ten 1x1, four 2x2, and one 3x3 square.
Only the two individual one cells form squares.
